title: Incident response, in order
scenario: Place the incident response phases in the order CompTIA defines them. The order is not administrative trivia: it is what makes the difference between containing an outbreak and cleaning hosts that are being reinfected while you work.
requirements: Partial credit applies per phase, so place every one even where you are unsure.

subtasks.label: Preparation first
subtasks.correctNote: Everything that makes a response possible happens before the incident: the plan, the tools, the training.

subtasks.label: Detection second
subtasks.correctNote: Detection is noticing something happened. It is not yet knowing what.

subtasks.label: Analysis third
subtasks.correctNote: Analysis establishes what it is and how far it has spread. Skipping it means containing a scope you guessed.

subtasks.label: Containment fourth
subtasks.correctNote: Stop the spread before removing anything. This is the one people move, and moving it is why outbreaks get re-cleaned all day.

subtasks.label: Eradication fifth
subtasks.correctNote: Remove the cause only once it can no longer spread.

subtasks.label: Recovery sixth
subtasks.correctNote: Return to service after the hole is closed, not before.

subtasks.label: Lessons learned last
subtasks.correctNote: The phase everyone skips, and the only one that stops a repeat.
